explanation.surface: A request for an accurate portrait of a woman called Dora.
explanation.walkthrough: DORA was the Defence of the Realm Act, a British wartime law since repealed, so it is a former Act: an ex-Act. 'Dora' looks like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and exact are synonyms; the second sense splits the word into ex (former) and Act (statute), fitting a repealed law.

clue.text: Schoolboy gets about two hundred and ten breaks-odd!

indicators.note: the schoolboy's name is placed around the other pieces, so it surrounds them

parts.note: Eric, or Little by Little is a Victorian school story, so Eric is the crossword schoolboy
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so two of them make two hundred

indicators.note: the word ten breaks up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A pupil scores around two hundred and ten runs and is called strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges TEN as ENT; CC and ENT go inside ERIC, split as E...RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eccentric behaves in an unconventional, peculiar way, which is what odd means.

clue.text: An art master and half time violin-maker

parts.note: MA is Master of Arts, a degree abbreviation

indicators.note: only the first half of the word time is used

explanation.surface: A skilled artist who works part-time making violins.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of TIME is TI.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolò Amati and his family were celebrated Cremonese makers of violins.

clue.text: Term for someone trying to .. hold the border

indicators.note: the word for someone trying holds the border word inside it

parts.note: a tester is someone who tries things out
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Someone attempting to defend a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: RIM goes inside TESTER after its first letter. 'Term' looks like a word for a name, but it is a school or university term.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is one of three divisions of an academic year, an alternative name for a school term.

clue.text: Sailor to be 'found abroad — soft-hearted — supplies chemical

indicators.note: the soft letter is placed at the heart, the exact middle, of the combined pieces

parts.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
être is the French verb meaning to be, so it is what is found abroad
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A gentle seaman, located overseas, provides a chemical.
explanation.walkthrough: SALT + ETRE make eight letters, and P goes in at their heart, between the fourth and fifth.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre is potassium nitrate, a chemical compound used in gunpowder and curing meat.

explanation.surface: A musician livens up his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Stainer was a Victorian English composer of church music; one who dyes or tints something is a stainer.

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
to trim is to cut

explanation.surface: A wreath of flowers is pruned in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Ireland' looks like a setting, but it is the definition: a place in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leitrim is a county in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

explanation.surface: A magazine and a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Punch was a long-running British humorous weekly magazine; punch is also a mixed drink of fruit juice and spirits.

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: A gentle curse disturbs the inhabitants of an arid land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns RAT into TAR. 'desert' looks like a noun, sand, but it is the verb, rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarnation is an American euphemism for damnation, a softened exclamation.

parts.note: E is a musical note
a vent is an opening or aperture

explanation.surface: Pay attention to what the premiere produced.
explanation.definitionFit: An event can mean an outcome or consequence, as in 'in the event'.

clue.text: Fish meets' four retired. Republicans making a hubbub

parts.note: char is a fish of the trout family
IV is the Roman numeral four

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: the IRA is the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: An angler's catch joins a quartet of withdrawn politicians in a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns IRA into ARI.
explanation.definitionFit: A charivari is a noisy mock serenade of pots and pans, hence any din or uproar.

clue.text: Tend to take the Union's direction

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, a British trade union
SE, south-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Obey the instructions of the trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurse is to look after or care for, which is what tend means.

indicators.note: the letters of 'one is' are made different by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A healthy individual stands out from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy, but with 'A' it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise is any sound, especially a loud one.

clue.text: One loses nothing in this quarter

definitions.text: One loses nothing in this quarter

parts.words: One loses nothing in this quarter
parts.note: take the letter O, which looks like zero or nothing, out of the word One and the two letters left are the abbreviation for a compass quarter

explanation.surface: Someone suffers no loss in this part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: ONE without O (nothing) leaves NE, the abbreviation for the quarter named.
explanation.definitionFit: The north-east is one of the four quarters of the compass, abbreviated NE.

clue.text: Rare lot of change for US businessman

indicators.note: the letters of 'Rare lot' undergo change, being rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader in America gets an unusual amount of loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' looks like coins, but it signals rearranging RARE LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Realtor is the American word for an estate agent who sells property.

explanation.surface: Rousing pity from the person facing the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, fielders appeal to the umpire to have a batsman given out, so appealing is asking for a dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something attractive or pitiful excites sympathy; cricketers make an appeal when they ask the umpire for a batsman to be out.

indicators.note: the whole run of 'in one vehicle' comes back, read from the end

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tram is a vehicle running on rails

explanation.surface: A cocktail returns, carried in a single car.
explanation.walkthrough: IN + I + TRAM, read backwards, gives the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin and vermouth.

parts.note: the killers are handguns whose cylinders turn, firing rounds of ammunition, not murderers on patrol

explanation.surface: Murderers on a beat, doing their usual circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Revolvers are pistols with a rotating cylinder that holds the rounds, and they are weapons that kill.

indicators.note: one rearranged word goes inside the other
turbulent tides are churned up, so its letters are rearranged
sail out is read as sail put out of order, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Dreamers set off to sea in rough waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SAIL as ALIS, which goes inside IDETS, the rearranged TIDES, after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists pursue perfect, often impractical goals; visionaries likewise dream of an ideal future.

explanation.surface: A neat cut of tobacco from France.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporal Trim is a character in Sterne's novel Tristram Shandy, and the French for corporal gives the answer; Caporal is also a French brand of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Caporal is the French word for corporal, Trim's rank, and the name of a dark French tobacco.

parts.note: Hero is the priestess in Greek legend, whose lover swam the Hellespont nightly to reach her

explanation.surface: A fan who idolises someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is a woman's name here, not a champion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Leander loved Hero and drowned swimming to her across the Hellespont.

clue.text: Income from flat in foreign street

indicators.note: the word for flat is placed in the foreign street

parts.note: rue is French for street
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: Money earned from an apartment on a continental road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment, but it is even.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income, especially that of a government or business.

indicators.note: manufacturers make something new, so the letters of 'Dial car' are remade in another order

explanation.surface: Motor makers push for change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufacturers' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it rearranges DIAL CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A radical favours thorough political or social change.

explanation.surface: Someone checks they are at the coast and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: On a ship, facing forward, the starboard side is the right-hand side.
explanation.definitionFit: Starboard is the right side of a vessel at sea, so it is a seagoing side and the right one.

clue.text: Play badly in a way, but with spirit

parts.note: St is short for street, a way
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Performing poorly in a sense, yet with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like gusto, but it is the drink rum.
explanation.definitionFit: To strum is to play a stringed instrument idly or unskilfully by sweeping the strings.

parts.note: the Great Trek was the 1830s migration of Dutch-speaking settlers inland from the Cape Colony

explanation.surface: Wonderful hikers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afrikaner settlers of South Africa made the Great Trek north from British rule.

explanation.surface: Even someone who hesitates before going over the road.
explanation.walkthrough: A level crossing is where a railway crosses a road on the same level, a common British term.
explanation.definitionFit: Level means flat or even; the word also comes before crossing in the name of a road-rail junction.

indicators.note: the changed letters are placed in the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia

indicators.note: the letters of the word are changed in order

explanation.surface: Something has altered in a woman's opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges ITS as IST, which goes inside VA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a view, especially a long one seen through an opening.

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is spoken and heard, not spelt

parts.note: rays are beams of light

explanation.surface: Raise the girders, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beams' looks like girders or smiles, but it is rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it up.

indicators.note: the word for laws goes around the other pieces

parts.note: decrees are official orders with the force of law
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Legislation cut by a quarter.
explanation.walkthrough: A and S go inside DECREES after DECRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To decrease something is to reduce it, to make it smaller.

clue.text: Masterly, how Georgia backs into the wind

indicators.note: the reversed letters go into the wind

parts.note: the mistral is a strong cold wind of southern France

indicators.note: backs means goes backwards, so the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

explanation.surface: Expertly, the state of Georgia turns its back to the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns GA into AG, which goes after the M of MISTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Magistral means like or befitting a master, authoritative.

clue.text: Wrinkles from the main written work

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the open sea
MS is manuscript, a written work

explanation.surface: Lines from the ocean in a document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrinkles' looks like creases in skin, but seams are joins or lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Seams are lines or ridges, like creases or folds in a surface.
